correctness.rationale: For all m>=3, states split exhaustively by center occupancy into U_h(A) (one missing arm) and V_{h,k} (center plus all but two leaves). All legal slides either toggle one coordinate within a Q_{m-1} or use a unique two-edge bridge at one-hot coordinate vertices. A target-distance potential is 1-Lipschitz across every edge, including bridge edges, and direct routes attain it; bridge states are handled through their two neighbors. Diameter upper bound 2m covers cube-cube, cube-bridge, bridge-bridge; diametral pair U_h([m]\{h,k}), U_k([m]\{h,k}) attains 2m. Two independently implemented enumeration/BFS checkers confirm the formulas for m=3..7 and m=3..9, respectively. All boundary cases m=3,4 are included.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the full explicit m-cube-plus-K_m-bridge isomorphism, its all-pairs closed metric, exact counts, diameter 2m and diameter pair with symmetric difference two. The 2014 tree result proves reachability and length bounds; the much closer 2018 spider result already constructs shortest paths for ALL spiders and therefore covers computational shortest-path existence on this family, but does not state this complete reconfiguration graph, the bridge architecture, count laws, or sharp global diameter. Avis-Hoang 2022 studies general structural decompositions but its inspected theorem/appendix does not present this specific cube network or global diameter. Indexed records include a subdivided-star independence/dissociation extremal claim with different invariant. Search cannot rule out an unindexed equivalent characterization.

value.rationale: Uniform depth-two stars are canonical trees with a central bottleneck. The theorem shows that an entire exponentially large configuration graph has a rigid m-cube/K_m bridge architecture and exact diameter 2m. Its extremal pair differs at only two leaf vertices yet requires a linearly growing number of moves because other tokens must clear the central bottleneck; this contrasts local configuration difference with global reconfiguration cost. Explicit metric and counts are useful benchmarks for general spider shortest-sequence algorithms and for structural TS_k decompositions. The value is in exact global geometry, not in re-proving algorithmic shortest-path solvability.
